title: Limits of a diagram inverting a pointwise reflection are computed on the reflective subcategory
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors, full subcategories, mapping spaces, cones, limiting cones and the coherent cone categories $(\Delta_K\downarrow F)$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and precomposition of mapping spaces with an edge as in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], in a fixed sufficiently large universe. Let $J$ be a small quasicategory and $\iota:A\hookrightarrow J$ the inclusion of a full subcategory. Suppose every object $j$ of $J$ admits an edge $u_j:j\to\iota(a_j)$ with $a_j\in A$ such that precomposition with $u_j$ induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_J(\iota(a_j),\iota(a))\to\operatorname{Map}_J(j,\iota(a))$ for every $a\in A$. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory and $\Gamma:J\to\mathcal C$ a coherent functor such that $\Gamma(u_j)$ is an equivalence for every $j$. Then restriction along $\iota$ induces an equivalence of coherent cone categories $(\Delta_J\downarrow\Gamma)\to(\Delta_A\downarrow\Gamma\iota)$. In particular a cone $\lambda:\Delta_Jx\to\Gamma$ is limiting if and only if its restriction $\lambda\iota$ is limiting, and $\Gamma$ has a limiting cone if and only if $\Gamma\iota$ has one. No limits in $\mathcal C$ are assumed, and $J$ may be empty.

Ordinary-category analogue: Mathlib CategoryTheory/Limits/Final.lean:144 initial_of_adjunction. Infinity-categorical reference (HTT section 4.1 / Kerodon cofinality) WANTED, not archived.

proof.text: Let $\iota:A\hookrightarrow J$ denote the given full inclusion. Fullness identifies $\operatorname{Map}_A(a,a')$ with $\operatorname{Map}_J(\iota a,\iota a')$. The supplied edge $u_j:j\to\iota(a_j)$ therefore satisfies exactly the universal-arrow hypothesis for the functor $\iota$: for every $a\in A$, precomposition with $u_j$ is the displayed equivalence. Applying [lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion] gives a coherent left adjoint $L:J\to A$, a unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}_J\to\iota L$, a counit $\epsilon:L\iota\to\mathrm{id}_A$, and the adjunction triangles, together with the natural mapping-space equivalences induced by $\eta$.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.6.1, local universal-arrow criterion; fullness is the definition of the stated full subcategory

proof.text: Compare any two universal arrows $v:j\to\iota(b)$ and $w:j\to\iota(c)$. Their mapping-space equivalences give edges $t:b\to c$ and $s:c\to b$ with $\iota(t)v\simeq w$ and $\iota(s)w\simeq v$. Associativity gives $\iota(st)v\simeq v$ and $\iota(ts)w\simeq w$. Injectivity on components of the respective universal mapping equivalences gives $[s][t]=1_b$ and $[t][s]=1_c$. By [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], $t,s$ are equivalences. Applying this to $v=\eta_j$, $w=u_j$ shows $\Gamma(u_j)\simeq\Gamma(\iota t)\Gamma(\eta_j)$ with $t$ an equivalence. Functors preserve inverse-triangle witnesses, so $\Gamma(\eta_j)$ is an equivalence. Also, for $j=\iota(a)$, the identity arrow to $\iota(a)$ is universal by fullness. Comparing it with $\eta_{\iota(a)}$ shows that this unit component is an equivalence. The triangle $\iota(\epsilon_a)\eta_{\iota(a)}\simeq1$ makes $\iota(\epsilon_a)$ its inverse. Fullness puts that inverse and its two witnessing triangles in $A$, so $\epsilon_a$ is an equivalence. These comparisons need only component bijections, not functorial choices of $t,s$.

source.place: Universal-arrow comparison written by the second reader from the mapping equivalences of 02F1 and the composition calculus of 01PF; the counit uses the first adjunction triangle.

proof.text: Put $\alpha=\Gamma\eta:\Gamma\to\Gamma\iota L$. By the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], it has a coherent inverse $\beta$ with inverse-triangle witnesses. Let $P_A=(\Delta_A\downarrow\Gamma\iota)$ and let $p:P_A\to\mathcal C$ be the apex projection. The pullback definition supplies a universal cone family on $A\times P_A\times\Delta^1$, from $p$ to $\Gamma\iota$. Whisker this family with $L$ and append $\beta$ (constant in $P_A$). These are a map $(J\times P_A)\times\Lambda_1^2\to\mathcal C$. The inner horn inclusion is inner anodyne by its defining lifting property. Apply [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product] with $\varnothing\hookrightarrow J\times P_A$ and fill against $\mathcal C\to\Delta^0$. The long edge defines a single simplicial family from $p$ to $\Gamma$, hence, by the explicit cone pullback, a functor $E:P_A\to(\Delta_J\downarrow\Gamma)$ over $\mathcal C$. On objects its formula is $E(\mu)=\beta\circ(\mu L)$. Its values on all simplices are restrictions of this one filler; no independently chosen pointwise composites are asserted to be functorial. Denote the restriction functor by $R$.

source.place: Lines 103-109, innerAnodyneExtensions_pushoutObjObjι', applied to the inner horn and the empty-to-parameter monomorphism; agent construction of the inverse cone functor.

proof.text:
For a cone $\lambda:\Delta_Jx\to\Gamma$, naturality along $\eta$ gives a square with equation $\alpha\lambda\simeq(\lambda\iota)L$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal C)$. Pasting $\beta$ gives
$$ER(\lambda)=\beta\circ(\lambda\iota)L\simeq\beta\alpha\lambda\simeq\lambda.$$
To retain the cone compatibilities, perform this pasting on the universal $J$-cone family, with its entire cone category as parameter. The square is the restriction of that evaluation family along $\eta$; the second homotopy is the chosen inverse triangle of $\beta,\alpha$. The composition and associativity fillings are supplied by [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine] and [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product]. Cancellation can be filled relative to the apex and the fixed $\Gamma$ endpoint by [lem-cbc-invertible-prism-extension]: the short edges being cancelled are $\alpha$ or $\beta$ at the diagram endpoint and identities at the apex, all equivalences. Thus the pasted homotopy is a coherent cone transformation $ER\simeq\mathrm{id}$ over the identity of the apex. Reversing the inverse triangles supplies its inverse. Using the full parameter family makes these transformations natural on morphisms and higher simplices, not only on cone objects.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.8 for cancellation prisms relative to their fixed faces; 01PF for coherent pasting. Agent calculation of E R from naturality along the unit.

proof.text:
For $\mu:\Delta_Ax\to\Gamma\iota$, naturality along $\epsilon:L\iota\to\mathrm{id}_A$ gives
$$\mu\simeq(\Gamma\iota\epsilon)\circ(\mu L\iota).$$
The first adjunction triangle gives $(\Gamma\iota\epsilon)\circ(\alpha\iota)\simeq1_{\Gamma\iota}$. Since $\alpha\iota$ is an equivalence with inverse $\beta\iota$, paste its inverse triangle on the right to get $\Gamma\iota\epsilon\simeq\beta\iota$. Consequently
$$RE(\mu)=(\beta\iota)\circ(\mu L\iota)\simeq\mu.$$
Use the universal $A$-cone family with parameter $P_A$ in this calculation. The naturality square comes from its evaluation on $\epsilon$, and the comparison of the two inverse edges comes from the specified adjunction triangle and the inverse triangle of $\alpha\iota$. The coherent composition, inner-prism and invertible-prism fillings cited here give the pasting relative to the apex and the fixed $\Gamma\iota$ endpoint. All short edges cancelled are equivalences by Step 2. Reversing these inverse homotopies gives the inverse cone transformation. This yields $RE\simeq\mathrm{id}$ as a coherent natural equivalence of cone functors. Together with Step 4, $E$ is a quasi-inverse to restriction.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.8 for the relative inverse/cancellation prisms; 02F1 and the adjunction triangle for the displayed comparison. Agent calculation of R E from naturality along the counit.

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], an equivalence of quasicategories induces equivalences on all mapping spaces. Hence the cone equivalence just constructed preserves and reflects terminal objects: essential surjectivity tests mapping spaces from every source, and a space equivalent to a contractible space is contractible. By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], terminal cones are exactly limiting cones. Thus every cone is limiting if and only if its restriction is, and a limiting cone exists on one side if and only if one exists on the other. If $J$ is empty, its full subcategory $A$ is empty, and both cone categories are canonically $\mathcal C$; restriction is the identity and a limit means a terminal object of $\mathcal C$, without assuming one exists. If $A$ is empty, the existence of $a_j$ in the hypotheses forces $J$ empty as well.
